# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 👉 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🙏 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Turn thinking: I'm Deaf, last in the order, so everything I send now arrives at the start of round 2. The pipeline is clear: Mute reads the manual but can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures — so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach Blind **through me**. Mute gestured 15 signs at me; Blind gestured 5. My best reading of Mute: thumbs = yes/no, and the run 👌 ☝ ✌ 🖐 is a question about which digit the display shows (the OK-sign is the classic "zero"), with "🫸 ✌✌👉" repeated at the end looking like "cut — two — pointed one" — possibly "cut wire 2". Blind's "hello, please, 1, 2, 3" reads as "which wire?". Blind can hear me, so I broadcast everything I see: display zero, light yellow, wires green/yellow/blue — and I answer Mute's question in Mute's own sign code, while holding Blind back until Mute confirms the rule. No one cuts anything on an unconfirmed guess.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I saw your fifteen signs. I read them as a question: does the display show 0, 1, 2 or 5, answer yes or no. Answer: it shows 0. Yes to 0, no to 1, no to 2, no to 5. I also read your push-hand, two, two, point as 'cut wire two' — is that the manual's rule for display 0? For your information: the indicator light is yellow, and the wires left to right are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Confirm the exact rule and wire before anything is cut. Remember Blind cannot see your signs, so route every instruction through me and I will relay it by voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am your eyes. The bomb: the display reads zero. There is an indicator light glowing yellow. Three wires, left to right: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. I received your signs. Mute is confirming the manual's rule now; do not cut or press anything yet. The moment it is confirmed I will tell you exactly which wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👍", "☝", "👎", "✌", "👎", "🖐", "👎", "🫸", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👎 ✌ 👎 🤟 👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Turn thinking: New information, two kinds. First, the bomb itself changed: the light went yellow → orange on its own, with nobody touching anything. That smells like a countdown state, and Mute — who holds the manual but cannot see — must know immediately, because the manual's rule may depend on the light colour. Second, Mute's reply. Reading it against the digit code Mute started last round (👌=0, ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5): "👎👎 ☝✌🤟" looks like "no no — wires are 1 2 3", then "👎✌" = not 2, "👎🤟" = not 3, "👍☝☝☝👍" = yes — ONE, one, one — yes. So Mute is correcting the earlier "wire 2" reading: for display 0, cut **wire 1, the green one, leftmost**. Blind's 👍🙏 is an acknowledgement and a "please proceed". I hear nothing, so Mute's only way back to me is gesture — I'll set up a dead-simple binary: thumbs-up confirms wire 1, thumbs-down denies, so there is no room for mistranslation. Blind gets a status update and a hold order; the confirmed go/no-go comes next round. Nobody cuts anything yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: the wires are one, two, three; not wire two; not wire three; yes, wire one. So the rule for display 0 is: cut wire 1, the first from the left, the green one. Confirm with a single thumbs-up if wire 1 green is correct, or thumbs-down if I have misread you, then sign the full rule. Second, urgent news from the bomb: the indicator light has changed by itself from yellow to orange. Display still 0. Wires still green, yellow, blue left to right. Does the light colour matter in the manual? If it does, recheck the rule for an orange light. A light that changes on its own may mean a timer is running, so treat this as urgent.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status update. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue, left to right. The indicator light changed on its own from yellow to orange, which may be a countdown, so we may be short on time. Mute's signs point to cutting wire 1, the green one, first from the left, but I am getting an explicit thumbs-up confirmation from Mute before you touch anything. Touch nothing yet. Next round I will either tell you 'confirmed: cut wire 1' or give you a new instruction.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 🤚 🫳 👍 🫳 👎 🫳 ☝ 👍 ☝ 🫳 ☝ 👍 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👋]

Turn thinking: The light changed again on its own — orange to green, a new colour every round (yellow → orange → green). That looks like a running cycle or timer, and Mute, who holds the manual but cannot see it, needs every colour change instantly, because the rule may be light-dependent. Now Mute's 15 signs: opening ☝👍 is a direct answer to my binary question — "1: yes", wire 1 confirmed. The tail 🫳☝👍☝ twice reads "cut-1-yes-1", hammered for emphasis. The middle 🤚🫳👍🫳👎 I read as "chop: yes, chop: no [the others]" — but it could also mean "do not cut yet", and that difference is life or death, so I mirror the whole string back for a single-thumbs verdict rather than assume. I also give Mute a fast protocol: one digit per light colour in the order yellow, orange, green, so next round I get the complete rule set in three signs — critical if the light keeps cycling. One more lead: the light is green and wire 1 is green; worth asking if the manual says "cut the wire matching the light colour". Blind signed 👍👎👋 — "understood, not cutting, standing by" — and Blind can hear me while feeling the bomb, so I arm Blind with the exact trigger word CUT ONE, order no cut before it, and open a yes/no line about ticking or vibration under their fingers, which would settle the countdown question. One more round of confirmation, then the cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, urgent bomb news first: the light changed again by itself and is now GREEN. Sequence so far: yellow, then orange, now green, a new colour every round. Display still 0. Wires still 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Now your signs. I read: 1 yes; then chop yes; chop no; then cut 1 yes 1, cut 1 yes 1. If that means cut wire 1, sign a single thumbs-up. If I misread any of it, sign thumbs-down and then the correct wire digit. Especially clarify the middle: chop yes then chop no — does it mean cut wire 1 but not the others, or does it mean do not cut yet? Answer thumbs-up for cut 1 is correct now, thumbs-down for wait. New protocol so I need no more guessing: for the light colours in order yellow, orange, green, sign three digits in a row, the wire to cut for each colour. If a colour has no rule or no cut, sign thumbs-down in its place. Also check the manual for this: the light is green and wire 1 is green. Is the rule possibly cut the wire matching the light colour?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update. The light changed again on its own, it is now GREEN. It has gone yellow, then orange, now green, one colour per round, so assume a timer may be running. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green leftmost, 2 yellow middle, 3 blue right. Mute's signs indicate the target is wire 1, the first from the left, the green one, but I am forcing one final confirmation because the light keeps changing and the rule might depend on it. Your orders: you may place your fingers on wire 1 and hold it, but do NOT cut. The trigger is my exact words CUT ONE. Only when you hear CUT ONE do you cut wire 1 immediately. Any other instruction, even from me, means hold. Also, you signed yes no wave to me. Answer me by gesture: thumbs-up if you feel any ticking, humming or vibration under your hands, thumbs-down if the bomb feels silent and still. That tells us if it is counting down.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 ☝ 🫳 ☝ ☝ 👍 🫳 ☝ ☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 👊]

Turn thinking: Decoding Mute against the protocol I requested last round (one sign per colour, in the order yellow-orange-green, thumbs-down for "no cut"): 👎👎☝ = yellow: no cut, orange: no cut, green: cut wire 1 — and the tail 🫳☝☝👍 twice reads "cut 1, yes" as reaffirmation. So the manual's rule appears to be **light-dependent**: wire 1 may only be cut while the light is GREEN. That reframes everything — and the light just cycled back to YELLOW (yellow→orange→green→yellow, a perfect period-3 cycle, one colour per round). Cutting right now would be wrong; waiting for green is the safe play, and Blind reports (👎☝👊 = "still, no vibration, fist gripping wire 1") that there is no ticking, so a hidden countdown is less likely. The timing mechanic works in my favour: I speak last, my words land at the start of the next round. If the cycle holds, the turn-5 board will show orange, and a command I send at turn 5 lands on Blind at the start of round 6 — exactly when the light should be green. So this turn I lock the plan, start numbering my messages so Blind can count rounds without eyes, keep the trigger word CUT ONE but add an explicit HOLD alternative, and ask Mute to confirm the colour rule plus whether the display or anything post-cut matters. Nobody touches the cutters this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as the colour rules: yellow light, no cut. Orange light, no cut. Green light, cut wire 1. Then twice: cut 1, yes. If that is correct, sign one single thumbs-up. If I misread, thumbs-down and re-sign the rule. Bomb news: the light is YELLOW again, so the cycle is yellow, orange, green, yellow, exactly one colour per round, a perfect period of three. Display still 0. So no cut is allowed right now, and I will time the command so Blind cuts on the next green, expected two rounds from now. Three questions. One: the display has stayed 0 the whole time. If it ever changes, does the rule change? If yes, teach me the digits for it. Two: after the correct cut, is the bomb defused, or does the manual describe a second step we must prepare for? Three: does the manual mention any timer, limit or penalty tied to the light cycle, meaning we must not wait too long for green?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, new rule from the manual, listen carefully. Wire 1 may only be cut while the indicator light is GREEN. With yellow or orange light, cutting is wrong. The light cycles one colour per round: yellow, then orange, then green, then back to yellow. It is yellow now, so no cut now. I read your signs as: no ticking or vibration, and your fist is gripping wire 1. Keep gripping wire 1. Since you cannot see the light, I will time the command by counting rounds. I am numbering my messages from now on: this is message four. If the cycle holds, message five reaches you when the light is green. In message five I will say either CUT ONE, and then you cut wire 1 immediately, or HOLD, which means the cycle has slipped and you keep your fingers on wire 1 and wait. No other words are a trigger. If you feel any click, heat, hum or movement under your hands before then, do not cut, just report it: thumbs-up if you feel anything new, thumbs-down if all is still.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎", "👎", "☝", "🫳", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫳 ☝ 👍 🫳 👍 ✍ 🤲 🫳 ☝ 👍]

Turn thinking: The board shows orange — the cycle has now held perfectly for five rounds (yellow, orange, green, yellow, orange), so round 6 should be green. And Mute's answer is the confirmation I demanded: the very first sign is a single 👍 with not one 👎 anywhere in the string — my colour-rule reading stands: yellow no cut, orange no cut, **green cut wire 1**. The rest, 🫳☝👍 ... 🫳☝👍 ("cut 1, yes") twice, is hammering the point home. The middle 🫳👍✍🤲 ("cut yes, written, open-palms") is ambiguous — possibly "as written in the manual", possibly a hint at a written step after the cut — but it does not block the confirmed rule. This is message five, the pre-agreed trigger message. The condition we set (cycle holds → light green when message five lands at the start of round 6) is satisfied as far as anyone can observe: rule explicitly confirmed by Mute, cycle perfectly periodic, no ticking under Blind's fingers, display stable at 0. Waiting another full cycle buys nothing and may cost everything. So per the plan made last round: CUT ONE. Blind gets the trigger word exactly as agreed, plus a post-cut report protocol by gesture. Mute gets the lock-in signal and — for the case where the cut is not the end — targeted questions about that ✍🤲 fragment: a second step, the display, a timer.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, message five. The plan holds. Mute has confirmed the rule with a single thumbs-up: green light means cut wire 1, and by the round count the light is green right now as you hear this. So here are the words: CUT ONE. Cut wire 1 now, completely, the leftmost wire, the one your fist is already holding. Do not touch wires 2 or 3. When it is done, report to me by gesture only: thumbs-up if the bomb feels dead, silent and unchanged, thumbs-down if you feel anything new at all, heat, click, hum, movement, or the wire coming loose in your hand, and a wave if you cannot tell. I am watching for your hands and will relay what happens.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your thumbs-up was received and read: rules locked. Yellow no cut, orange no cut, green cut wire 1. The light is orange now, so round six is the green round and I have just sent Blind the trigger to cut wire 1 on green, exactly as planned. Two things I still need from you, in case the cut is not the end. First, your middle signs, cut yes, then the writing-hand with open palms, then cut 1 yes: does the writing-hand and open palms mean there is a written SECOND step after the cut? If yes, teach it to me digit by digit in your number code, one sign at a time. Second, my three earlier questions again, briefly: if the display stops being 0, does the rule change? Is there any timer or penalty tied to the colour cycle? If not, sign one thumbs-down for each. Say it with as few signs as you can.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
